newsitem.title: USA: McCrory to close stores in cost-cutting effort.
newsitem.headline: McCrory to close stores in cost-cutting effort.

text.p: McCrory Corp, a retailer operating under Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection since 1992, on Wednesday said it planned a "comprehensive store closing" program and a review of its operations to cut costs.
The moves came after the company failed to meet a provision of its credit agreement with CIT Group/Business Credit, it said.
The company said it failed to meet its projection of a 15 percent sales increase in December. Revenue generated during the month was little changed from the same month of 1995, it said.
Details about the planned store closings and the company's sales were not immediately available.
Company officials could not be immediately reached for further comment.

McCrory said it defaulted on the so-called clean-up requirement of its credit agreement with CIT. That stipulated that the retailer's outstanding debt excluding letters of credit under the facility must not exceed $30 million on December 31, 1996.
The company's total debt excluding letters of credit was about $52 million, McCrory said.
CIT and McCrory are working to improve the retailer's near-term liquidity, and the companies are in talks about financing after McCrory satisfies the clean-up requirement.
